---
title: "HB Temporal C Synthesis: General trend workflow (linear vs segmented vs non-linear)"
author: "Caitlin Hicks Pries"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---
#Purpose
A reusable workflow for any annual table with a year column, one or more numeric variables, and optional grouping columns (site, watershed, elevation group, horizon, etc.).

For every variable x group (a "series") it fits three models, **all with AR(1) errors** (generalized least squares, `nlme::gls`), so year-to-year autocorrelation is accounted for in the slopes, p-values and AIC:

1. **Linear trend:** slope, standard error, p-value, standardized slope, R2, and the estimated AR(1) autocorrelation (`ar1_phi`)
2. **Segmented regression** (one breakpoint, found by grid search, then refit with AR(1) errors): breakpoint year, slope before and after, p-values, and a Davies test (`segmented` package) for whether a breakpoint exists
3. **Natural spline** (smooth non-linear curve, `spline_df = 3` by default) as the non-linear alternative, with a likelihood-ratio test of curvature against the straight line
4. **Model comparison by AIC:** the linear model is kept unless an alternative has an AIC at least 2 lower

To use it on a new variable or dataset, only change the arguments of `analyze_trends()` in the examples below. The functions are defined once in the "Functions" chunk.

#Setup
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls()) #clear R environment

# Check for and install required packages and load libraries
for (package in c('tidyverse', 'here')) {    #can add more packages to this vector
  if (!require(package, character.only=T, quietly=T)) {
    install.packages(package)
    library(package, character.only=T)
  }
}

#These two are only called with package::function(), so they are installed but NOT attached.
#(Attaching segmented also attaches MASS, which masks dplyr::select().)
for (package in c('nlme', 'segmented')) {
  if (!requireNamespace(package, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(package)
}

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here())
```

#Functions
Run this chunk once; nothing in it needs to be edited.

* `analyze_trends()`: returns one row per variable x group with all the statistics below
* `plot_trend_fits()`: one panel per group showing the data, the linear fit (dashed black), a natural spline curve (red), and the breakpoint (dotted blue) where the segmented model is best

**Standardized slope:** `lin_std_slope` is the slope in standard-deviation units of both variable and year (slope x sd(year) / sd(variable)), the same as `lm(scale(y) ~ scale(year))`. It lets you compare variables with different units, but because it depends on how long the record is, compare it across series of different lengths with care. `lin_slope_sd_per_yr` (slope / sd(variable)) is the change in standard deviations per year and is easier to compare across records of different lengths.
```{r functions}
#Convert a Date (floor date) or numeric year to a numeric year
to_year <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, c("Date", "POSIXct"))) as.numeric(format(x, "%Y")) else as.numeric(x)
}

#Build a text label for each series from the grouping columns
make_series <- function(d, group_cols) {
  if (length(group_cols) == 0) return(rep("all", nrow(d)))
  do.call(paste, c(as.list(d[group_cols]), sep = " | "))
}

#Reshape to long format, apply the time window, and make sure there is one value per series per year
prep_long <- function(data, value_cols, group_cols = character(0), time_col = "year",
                      start_year = NULL, end_year = NULL) {
  stopifnot(all(c(value_cols, group_cols, time_col) %in% names(data)))

  out <- data %>%
    mutate(yr = to_year(.data[[time_col]])) %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(value_cols), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
    filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(yr))

  if (!is.null(start_year)) out <- filter(out, yr >= start_year)
  if (!is.null(end_year))   out <- filter(out, yr <= end_year)

  #more than one row per series per year (e.g. several horizons in one horizon type) gets averaged
  dupes <- out %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_cols, "variable", "yr")))) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n > 1)
  if (nrow(dupes) > 0) {
    message("Note: ", nrow(dupes), " series-year combinations had more than one row and were averaged. ",
            "If that is not what you want, add the missing column (e.g. Horizon) to group_cols.")
  }

  out %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_cols, "variable", "yr")))) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
}

#Fit a model with AR(1) errors (generalized least squares). Returns NULL if it can't be fit.
#"ML" is used for AIC and model comparison; "REML" gives better slope standard errors.
gls_ar1 <- function(formula, data, method = "ML") {
  tryCatch(
    nlme::gls(formula, data = data,
              correlation = nlme::corAR1(form = ~ yr), method = method),
    error = function(e) NULL)
}

#Fit all models for ONE series (d has columns yr and value). All models have AR(1) errors.
fit_one <- function(d, min_years = 10, min_seg = 5, spline_df = 3) {
  d <- d %>% arrange(yr)
  n <- nrow(d)

  #template row: every column exists even if a model can't be fit
  res <- tibble(
    n_years = n, first_year = min(d$yr), last_year = max(d$yr),
    mean_value = mean(d$value), sd_value = sd(d$value),
    ar1_phi = NA_real_,
    lin_slope = NA_real_, lin_se = NA_real_, lin_p = NA_real_,
    lin_std_slope = NA_real_, lin_slope_sd_per_yr = NA_real_, lin_r2 = NA_real_,
    seg_breakpoint = NA_real_, seg_slope_before = NA_real_, seg_slope_before_p = NA_real_,
    seg_slope_after = NA_real_, seg_slope_after_p = NA_real_,
    seg_std_before = NA_real_, seg_std_after = NA_real_, seg_change_p_naive = NA_real_,
    seg_davies_p = NA_real_,
    spline_p_curvature = NA_real_,
    AIC_linear = NA_real_, AIC_segmented = NA_real_, AIC_spline = NA_real_,
    best_model = NA_character_, delta_AIC_vs_linear = NA_real_,
    note = NA_character_
  )

  if (n < min_years || isTRUE(sd(d$value) == 0)) return(res)

  sx <- sd(d$yr); sy <- sd(d$value)

  #---- 1. Linear with AR(1) errors ----
  lin_ml   <- gls_ar1(value ~ yr, d, "ML")
  lin_reml <- gls_ar1(value ~ yr, d, "REML")
  if (is.null(lin_ml) || is.null(lin_reml)) {
    res$note <- "linear AR(1) model did not fit"
    return(res)
  }
  tt <- summary(lin_reml)$tTable
  res$ar1_phi             <- as.numeric(coef(lin_reml$modelStruct$corStruct, unconstrained = FALSE))
  res$lin_slope           <- tt["yr", "Value"]
  res$lin_se              <- tt["yr", "Std.Error"]
  res$lin_p               <- tt["yr", "p-value"]
  res$lin_std_slope       <- tt["yr", "Value"] * sx / sy
  res$lin_slope_sd_per_yr <- tt["yr", "Value"] / sy
  res$lin_r2              <- cor(as.numeric(fitted(lin_reml)), d$value)^2   #squared correlation of fitted and observed
  res$AIC_linear          <- AIC(lin_ml)

  #---- 2. Segmented (one breakpoint) with AR(1) errors ----
  #The breakpoint is chosen by a grid search over observed years (ordinary least squares,
  #at least min_seg points on each side), then the model is refit with AR(1) errors.
  if (n >= 2 * min_seg + 1) {
    #Davies test: is there evidence for a breakpoint anywhere in the record? It allows for the
    #breakpoint having been searched for. It uses ordinary least squares, so it assumes independent errors.
    #do.call() puts the data into the call, which segmented needs when d is created inside a function.
    res$seg_davies_p <- tryCatch(
      segmented::davies.test(do.call("lm", list(formula = value ~ yr, data = d)),
                             seg.Z = ~ yr)$p.value,
      error = function(e) NA_real_)

    cand <- d$yr[min_seg:(n - min_seg)]
    rss  <- vapply(cand, function(bp) {
      sum(resid(lm(value ~ yr + pmax(yr - bp, 0), data = d))^2)
    }, numeric(1))
    bp <- cand[which.min(rss)]
    d$hinge <- pmax(d$yr - bp, 0)

    seg_ml   <- gls_ar1(value ~ yr + hinge, d, "ML")
    seg_reml <- gls_ar1(value ~ yr + hinge, d, "REML")

    if (!is.null(seg_ml) && !is.null(seg_reml)) {
      b   <- coef(seg_reml); V <- vcov(seg_reml); tts <- summary(seg_reml)$tTable
      s_after  <- unname(b["yr"] + b["hinge"])
      se_after <- sqrt(V["yr", "yr"] + V["hinge", "hinge"] + 2 * V["yr", "hinge"])
      res$seg_breakpoint     <- bp
      res$seg_slope_before   <- unname(b["yr"])
      res$seg_slope_before_p <- tts["yr", "p-value"]
      res$seg_slope_after    <- s_after
      res$seg_slope_after_p  <- 2 * pt(-abs(s_after / se_after), df = n - 3)
      res$seg_std_before     <- unname(b["yr"]) * sx / sy
      res$seg_std_after      <- s_after * sx / sy
      res$seg_change_p_naive <- tts["hinge", "p-value"]   #optimistic, see notes
      res$AIC_segmented      <- AIC(seg_ml) + 2           #+2 for the estimated breakpoint
    } else {
      res$note <- paste(na.omit(c(res$note, "segmented AR(1) model did not fit")), collapse = "; ")
    }
  }

  #---- 3. Natural spline (smooth non-linear curve, fixed df) with AR(1) errors ----
  #the df number is written into the formula text, because nlme::gls cannot find a variable
  #(spline_df) that is not a column in the data
  spl_formula <- as.formula(paste0("value ~ splines::ns(yr, df = ", spline_df, ")"))
  spl_ml <- gls_ar1(spl_formula, d, "ML")
  if (!is.null(spl_ml)) {
    res$AIC_spline <- AIC(spl_ml)
    #likelihood-ratio test: is the curve better than a straight line? (linear is nested in the spline)
    res$spline_p_curvature <- tryCatch(anova(lin_ml, spl_ml)[["p-value"]][2],
                                       error = function(e) NA_real_)
  } else {
    res$note <- paste(na.omit(c(res$note, "spline AR(1) model did not fit")), collapse = "; ")
  }

  #---- 4. Choose the model: linear unless an alternative is >= 2 AIC units better ----
  alt <- c(segmented = res$AIC_segmented, spline = res$AIC_spline)
  alt <- alt[!is.na(alt)]
  if (length(alt) > 0) {
    res$delta_AIC_vs_linear <- res$AIC_linear - min(alt)   #positive = alternative fits better
    res$best_model <- if (res$delta_AIC_vs_linear >= 2) names(which.min(alt)) else "linear"
  } else {
    res$best_model <- "linear"
  }
  res
}

trend_short <- function(data, value_cols, group_cols = character(0), time_col = "year",
                        start_year = NULL, end_year = NULL, min_years = 5, max_years = 9) {

  prep_long(data, value_cols, group_cols, time_col, start_year, end_year) %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c("variable", group_cols)))) %>%
    filter(n() >= min_years, n() <= max_years, sd(value) > 0) %>%   # keep only the short series
    group_modify(~ {
      m  <- lm(value ~ yr, data = .x)
      cf <- summary(m)$coefficients
      kt <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(.x$yr, .x$value, method = "kendall"))
      tibble(
        n_years = nrow(.x), first_year = min(.x$yr), last_year = max(.x$yr),
        mean_value = mean(.x$value), sd_value = sd(.x$value),
        lin_slope = cf["yr", "Estimate"], lin_se = cf["yr", "Std. Error"],
        lin_p = cf["yr", "Pr(>|t|)"],
        lin_std_slope = cf["yr", "Estimate"] * sd(.x$yr) / sd(.x$value),
        lin_slope_sd_per_yr = cf["yr", "Estimate"] / sd(.x$value),
        lin_r2 = summary(m)$r.squared,
        kendall_tau = unname(kt$estimate), kendall_p = kt$p.value,
        best_model = "linear",
        note = "short series: linear OLS only, no autocorrelation adjustment")
    }) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(series = make_series(., group_cols)) %>%
    relocate(variable, series, all_of(group_cols))
}

#Main function: all variables x all groups
analyze_trends <- function(data, value_cols, group_cols = character(0), time_col = "year",
                           start_year = NULL, end_year = NULL, min_years = 10, min_seg = 5, spline_df = 3) {
  long <- prep_long(data, value_cols, group_cols, time_col, start_year, end_year)

  res <- long %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c("variable", group_cols)))) %>%
    group_modify(~ fit_one(.x, min_years, min_seg, spline_df)) %>%
    ungroup()

  if (all(is.na(res$lin_p))) stop("No series had at least ", min_years, " years of data.")

  res$series <- make_series(res, group_cols)

  res %>%
    group_by(variable) %>%
    mutate(lin_p_adj = p.adjust(lin_p, method = "BH")) %>%   #false discovery rate across series within a variable
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(lin_sig = case_when(is.na(lin_p) ~ NA_character_,
                               lin_p < 0.001 ~ "***",
                               lin_p < 0.01  ~ "**",
                               lin_p < 0.05  ~ "*",
                               TRUE          ~ "ns")) %>%
    relocate(variable, series, all_of(group_cols))
}

#Plot one variable: one panel per series
plot_trend_fits <- function(data, value_col, group_cols = character(0), time_col = "year",
                            results = NULL, start_year = NULL, end_year = NULL, min_years = 10, spline_df = 3) {
  d <- prep_long(data, value_col, group_cols, time_col, start_year, end_year)
  d$series <- make_series(d, group_cols)
  d <- d %>% group_by(series) %>% filter(n() >= min_years) %>% ungroup()

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = yr, y = value)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
                color = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = as.formula(paste0("y ~ splines::ns(x, df = ", spline_df, ")")), se = FALSE,
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~ series, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Year", y = value_col,
         title = paste(value_col, "- linear (dashed) vs spline (red); dotted line = breakpoint")) +
    theme_classic()

  if (!is.null(results)) {
    bp <- results %>% filter(.data$variable == value_col, .data$best_model == "segmented")
    if (nrow(bp) > 0) {
      p <- p + geom_vline(data = bp, aes(xintercept = seg_breakpoint),
                          linetype = "dotted", color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8)
    }
  }
  p
}

plot_trend_fits_short <- function(data, value_col, group_cols = character(0), time_col = "year",
                                  results = NULL, start_year = NULL, end_year = NULL,
                                  min_years = 5, max_years = 9) {

  d <- prep_long(data, value_col, group_cols, time_col, start_year, end_year)
  d$series <- make_series(d, group_cols)
  d <- d %>%
    group_by(series) %>%
    filter(n() >= min_years, n() <= max_years) %>%    # same window as trend_short()
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(d) == 0) stop("No series with ", min_years, " to ", max_years, " years of data.")

  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x = yr, y = value)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.8, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
                color = "black", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = function(x) unique(round(pretty(x)))) +   # whole years only
    facet_wrap(~ series, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Year", y = value_col,
         title = paste(value_col, "- linear trend only (short series)")) +
    theme_classic()
  p
}
```

#Example: pH and nitrate, 1980 to present
`value_cols` can be any numeric columns in the table, and `group_cols` can be any columns that define a series (site, watershed, elevation group, horizon). Use `character(0)` for a table with no groups (stream).

This section assumes the `annual_tables` list from `read_all_outputs` is in your environment, including the combined `Lysimeter_annual` table with the Site factor. If `year` is not a Date or number, convert it first.
```{r examples}
start_year <- 1980

#Precipitation, one series, could be multiple per rain gauge
atm_trends <- analyze_trends(
  annual_tables$AtmPrecipChem_annual_calendaryear,
  value_cols = c("pH_mean", "DOC_mean"),
  start_year = start_year) %>%
  mutate(dataset = "Precipitation", .before = 1) #label

#Soil solution, one series per watershed x horizon type
#(horizons within a type are averaged; use group_cols = c("Site", "Horizon") to keep them separate)
lys_trends <- analyze_trends(
  annual_tables$Lysimeter_annual,
  value_cols = c("pH_mean", "DOC_mean"),
  group_cols = c("Site", "Horizon_type"),
  start_year = start_year) %>%
  mutate(dataset = "Soil solution", .before = 1)

#Soil, one series per elevation x horizon type
#(horizons within a type are averaged; use group_cols = c("Site", "Horizon") to keep them separate)
soil_trends <- analyze_trends(
  annual_tables$SoilMicrobialBiomass_annual,
  value_cols = c("pH_mean", "BIOC_mean"),
  group_cols = c("Hor"), #could have elevation but is currently weird
  start_year = start_year) %>%
  mutate(dataset = "Soil", .before = 1)

#Soil gas
soilgas_trends <- analyze_trends(
  annual_tables$SoilGasFlux_annual,
  value_cols = c("CO2_rate_mean", "CH4_rate_mean"),
  group_cols = c("Site"), #could have elevation but is currently weird
  start_year = start_year) %>%
  mutate(dataset = "SoilGas", .before = 1)

#Stream W6, a single series
stream_trends <- analyze_trends(
  annual_tables$StreamChemW6_VWM_annual,
  value_cols = c("pH_vwm", "DOC_vwm", "DIC_vwm"),
  group_cols = character(0),
  start_year = start_year) %>%
  mutate(dataset = "Stream W6", .before = 1)

#Plants
AG_trends <- trend_short(
  annual_tables$AGBiomass_annual,
  value_cols = c("above_L_Mg_ha_mean"),
  group_cols = c("watershed"),
  start_year = start_year) %>%
  mutate(dataset = "AG", .before = 1)

litter_trends <- analyze_trends(
  annual_tables$Litterfall_annual,
  value_cols = c("avg_litter"),
  group_cols = c("site"),
  start_year = start_year) %>%
  mutate(dataset = "litter", .before = 1)

trend_results <- bind_rows(atm_trends, lys_trends, stream_trends)

#Compact view: linear trend and which model fits best
trend_results %>%
  select(dataset, variable, series, n_years, first_year, last_year,
         lin_slope, lin_std_slope, lin_p, lin_p_adj, lin_sig,
         best_model, delta_AIC_vs_linear, seg_breakpoint, seg_slope_before, seg_slope_after)
```

#Template for any other variable or grouping
Copy and change the four arguments. For elevation groups, put the elevation column in `group_cols` (for example `group_cols = c("site", "Elev_group")`).
```{r template, eval=FALSE}
my_trends <- analyze_trends(
  annual_tables$YOUR_TABLE,                 #any annual table
  value_cols = c("variable_1", "variable_2"),   #numeric columns to analyze
  group_cols = c("site", "Elev_group"),     #columns that define a series (or character(0))
  time_col   = "year",                      #Date (floor date) or numeric year column
  start_year = 1980,                        #optional time window
  min_years  = 10                           #series with fewer years are skipped
)
```

Check the fits visually before trusting the numbers.
```{r graph fits, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$AtmPrecipChem_annual_calendaryear, "pH_mean",
                results = atm_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$AtmPrecipChem_annual_calendaryear, "DOC_mean",
                results = atm_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$Lysimeter_annual, "pH_mean", c("Site", "Horizon_type"),
                results = lys_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$Lysimeter_annual, "DOC_mean", c("Site", "Horizon_type"),
                results = lys_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$StreamChemW6_VWM_annual, "pH_vwm",
                results = stream_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$StreamChemW6_VWM_annual, "DOC_vwm",
                results = stream_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$StreamChemW6_VWM_annual, "DIC_vwm",
                results = stream_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$SoilMicrobialBiomass_annual, "pH_mean", "Hor",
                results = soil_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$SoilMicrobialBiomass_annual, "BIOC_mean", "Hor",
                results = soil_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$SoilGasFlux_annual, "CO2_rate_mean", "Site",
                results = soilgas_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$SoilGasFlux_annual, "CH4_rate_mean", "Site",
                results = soilgas_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits(annual_tables$Litterfall_annual, "avg_litter", "site",
                results = litter_trends, start_year = start_year)

plot_trend_fits_short(annual_tables$AGBiomass_annual, "above_L_Mg_ha_mean", "watershed",
                results = litter_trends, start_year = start_year)
```

#Save the results
```{r save results}
dir.create(here("Trend_results"), showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(trend_results, here("Trend_results", "trend_results.csv"))
```

#Notes on interpreting the results
* **Autocorrelation is built in.** All models have AR(1) errors, so `lin_p` and the AIC values account for year-to-year dependence. `ar1_phi` is the estimated lag-1 autocorrelation. It is poorly estimated and biased toward zero in short series (under about 20 years), so treat p-values as a guide. If a model cannot be fit, the `note` column says which one.
* **lin_p_adj** corrects for testing many series (Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate, within each variable). `lin_sig` is based on the uncorrected p, so check `lin_p_adj` too.
* **The segmented p-values are still optimistic** because the breakpoint was chosen to fit the data best (AR(1) errors reduce but do not remove this; in simulations with no true breakpoint, about 20% of autocorrelated series still showed one by the AIC rule). `seg_davies_p` is the better test of whether a breakpoint exists, because the Davies test allows for the search, but it assumes independent errors, so it is still too liberal for autocorrelated series. Look for agreement: a breakpoint is most believable when `best_model` is segmented **and** `seg_davies_p` is small. `seg_change_p_naive` (the test of a change in slope) ignores that, so use `best_model` and `delta_AIC_vs_linear` (which already counts the breakpoint as an extra parameter) to decide if a breakpoint is supported.
* **delta_AIC_vs_linear:** positive means an alternative fits better than the line, and 2 or more is used as the cutoff. Differences of 2-4 are weak evidence; above about 10 is strong.
* **A breakpoint at the edge of the record** (within a few years of the first or last year) is poorly constrained. `min_seg` sets the minimum number of years on each side (default 5).
* **Spline:** `spline_p_curvature` tests whether the curve is better than a straight line. The spline can describe curvature but, unlike the segmented model, doesn't give a single change point. Change `spline_df` in `analyze_trends()` for a stiffer (2) or more flexible (4) curve; keep it at 3 or below for series under 25 years.
* **Short records:** with 10-15 years the alternative models can overfit and the AR(1) fit can fail to converge, so be cautious about `best_model` for short series.
